definition: PARRY was an early example of a chatbot, implemented in 1972 by psychiatrist Kenneth Colby.
details: PARRY was an early example of a chatbot, implemented in 1972 by psychiatrist Kenneth Colby.

explainer.lead: PARRY is an early chatbot, implemented in 1972 by psychiatrist Kenneth Colby. It stands as one of the first conversational programs, predating modern dialogue systems by decades.

tiers.eli5: It is a very old computer program from 1972 that could hold a simple typed conversation.
tiers.practitioner: PARRY is cited in the history of conversational AI and dialogue-system design. Its era gives no modern deployment guidance, so it is referenced as precedent rather than as a technique to reuse.
tiers.paperLevel: The documented record is attribution and date: a chatbot implemented in 1972 by psychiatrist Kenneth Colby. No further formal specification is given.

explainer.example: A course on the history of chatbots introduces PARRY alongside other early conversational programs from the 1960s and 1970s.
